elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence" — an affirmative maintenance covenant on HDI ("HDI shall maintain, at its own expense, during the term ... and for one (1) year thereafter"). Dollar sign rather than "USD" is cosmetic in a US-law agreement.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Same sentence continues "and $2,000,000 in the aggregate", tied to the CGL policy line.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $2,000,000" — meets the preferred limit exactly.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: "where HDI processes the Company's Confidential Information or user data, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than $5,000,000". The trigger is defined by reference to existing Section 8.1 subject matter (Content, user information, data), and it is engaged on these facts because HDI hosts the Site and handles user information.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: "and workers' compensation insurance as required by law" is carried by the same "HDI shall maintain" operative verb.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Final sentence: "HDI shall provide the Company with certificates of insurance upon request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O is written at not less than $2,000,000, which exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cyber and privacy liability is written at not less than $5,000,000, above the USD 2,000,000 floor; the "where HDI processes ... Confidential Information or user data" condition is satisfied on these facts (HDI hosts the Site and handles user information under Section 8.1), so the coverage is live.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements appear in a single operative covenant with the correct limits, the conditional cyber trigger, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request. The fallback checklist is also satisfied a fortiori.

The finding classification 'missing' is supported: the cited General Provisions run to 10.8 Headings; Counterparts with no insurance, coverage or policy covenant anywhere, and the vendor hosts the Site and processes user data, so the gap sits in walk-away territory rather than at the fallback.

Minimal: one concise new paragraph inserted after 10.8 in General Provisions; no existing text is deleted or altered, no operative term is duplicated (there is no pre-existing insurance language to conflict with), and the ancillary wording ('at its own expense', one-year tail) tracks the playbook model language rather than adding requirements outside the checklist.

Preserves intent: nothing in the insertion touches liability allocation, fees, term, termination or any other commercial mechanic; the covenant runs only against HDI and imposes no reciprocal customer obligation.

Two cosmetic points the drafter may wish to tidy, neither of which affects completeness: the inserted paragraph is rendered as 'Insurance.' without the '10.9' number promised in the rationale, and limits are stated with '$' rather than 'USD'. Under Section 10.8 headings have no interpretive effect, so neither weakens the covenant.

Margin comment complies with tone: it states what was added, why (no insurance covenant despite hosting and handling user information), and offers the E&O $1,000,000 / cyber $2,000,000 fallback without lecturing.
